players.product: synthetic DNA, proteins, antibody libraries, and characterization data

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: NGS applications revenue grew 12% year over year and 8% sequentially, driven by growth in top accounts; the top 10 NGS applications customers accounted for approximately 48% of NGS applications revenue, and Twist served 657 NGS applications customers in the quarter, 182 having adopted its products. Diagnostics revenue was $43.8 million versus $38.1 million a year earlier, up 15%, and grew 10% sequentially on strong growth in top accounts. CEO: NGS applications momentum is driven primarily by diagnostic customers, many growing commercial volumes and others advancing towards commercialization.
quarterly_data.figure: NGS applications +12% YoY, +8% QoQ; top 10 customers ~48% of NGS revenue; 657 NGS customers; Diagnostics $43.8M (+15%, +10% QoQ)

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Academic and government revenue was $15.5 million, up 32% year over year and 21% sequentially, driven by U.S. accounts where several large customers returned; industry and applied revenue was $5.7 million versus $6.1 million; global supply partner revenue was $12.9 million versus $13 million. By region, Americas revenue rose to $77.3 million from $59.4 million (+30%), EMEA to $33.6 million from $30.7 million (+9%) and APAC to $7.5 million from $5.9 million (+26%).
quarterly_data.figure: Academic & government $15.5M (+32%); industry & applied $5.7M; global supply partners $12.9M; Americas $77.3M (+30%); EMEA $33.6M (+9%); APAC $7.5M (+26%)

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance: for Q4 FY2026 Twist expects total revenue of $123 million to $124 million, growth of approximately 25% year over year at the midpoint, with sequential growth in both DSPS (driven by therapeutics) and NGS applications, and NGS expected to return to growth above 20% year over year. It expects gross margin above 52% for fiscal 2026, with a goal of more than 60% as the business matures, and expects to achieve adjusted EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY2026 and to maintain this commitment for fiscal 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 revenue $123M-$124M (~25% YoY); FY2026 gross margin above 52%; long-term gross margin goal more than 60%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: gross margin of 52.8% rose 120 basis points sequentially, with 70% of incremental revenue dropping to the gross margin line. Operating expenses excluding cost of revenues were $98.7 million versus $81.4 million, including approximately $2 million of employee transition costs and other one-time expenses, which will result in a more than $5 million reduction in OpEx in Q4. Adjusted EBITDA was a loss of approximately $11.3 million, and cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $166.8 million versus $171.7 million at March 31, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: gross margin +120 bps QoQ; OpEx $98.7M; adjusted EBITDA loss ~$11.3M; cash $166.8M

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the serviceable addressable market is projected to be $13 billion by 2030, and management believes it has a strong growth trajectory to more than double revenue from organic growth by 2031. Growth drivers named: AI-enabled drug discovery, molecular residual disease (MRD) with the reimbursement environment expanding, proprietary enzymes in its workflows and internal processes to optimize performance and cost and reduce dependence on suppliers, and, longer term, nucleic acid therapeutics.
quarterly_data.figure: SAM $13 billion by 2030; revenue to more than double organically by 2031

quarterly_data.signal: President and COO: Twist has built differentiated enzymes using AI-driven discovery and development methods, a high-performing ligase and a high-fidelity polymerase used in whole genome and other workflows, both featured in its kits and benchmarking well internally and in customers' hands. In MRD, tumor-informed platforms need more probes derived from sequencing the patient's tumor for higher sensitivity, and Twist sees demand increasing; it envisions future demand of hundreds of thousands to millions of tests, each needing thousands of probes delivered within a couple of days, which its synthesis platform and throughput position it to serve.

President and COO: during the early access of its complex genes offering (high GC content, repetitive or otherwise complex constructs made on the standard and express gene production line), a select handful of customers ordered more than 1,800 complex genes across well over 100 orders, with the overwhelming majority completed in 12 days; Twist formally launched the complex genes offering two weeks before the call, expanding availability broadly across the market.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 1,800 complex genes; well over 100 orders; 12 days

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in the hemorrhagic fever outbreak announced in the Democratic Republic of Congo on May 15, 2026, which escaped standard PCR assays, researchers used the Twist comprehensive viral panel approximately 1 month into the outbreak to identify the pathogen as the Bundibugyo Ebola virus; separately, Twist synthesized hantavirus material in less than 24 hours to support rapid response efforts during a cruise ship outbreak in May.
